Serial constraints cleared: `engine.ts`'s landings today (#6697, #6786, #6788, #6794, #6812, #6818) are ALL MERGED; in-flight in this lane: none (batch:1). #6745 is claimed by the `domain:cli` seat's session (`os-project-manager`) and is a metadata-service pin — no overlap with the autonumber region, but the dispatch requires merging `origin/main` before the PR regardless.
Carried rulings (⛔ do not relitigate — from #5495's 2026-08-07 disposition, restated in this card's body): plan **B** — keep the global counter, make seeding/resync correct; tenant-partitioning stays **parked** (PROBE4 measured that partition-seeding on driver-mongodb *creates* duplicates against its single-field global unique index, and #3724 refuses multi-tenant boot there); read failures during seeding must preserve #6114's `isMissingTableError` discrimination — ⛔ never swallow a read failure into 0/stale (#5979 family line).
Open to the implementer's measurement (this is the card's real question): **which resync shape is correct** — re-seed on collision, or re-seed on first write after an exempt-writer insert, or both — judged against `seedAutonumber`'s #6468 anchoring rules. The dispatch asks for the measurement, not a guess; if the correct shape needs #6250's predicate, report that as the dependency rather than hand-rolling one.
Container judgment: size M ⇒ `mode:cloud`.

Not a claim — this card is yours (`session_01MwoubC3jL271FYt9rGXwxb`, branch `claude/issue-6806-engine-autonumber-reseed`). The devx PM seat dispatched this card by mistake without reading the `domain:` routing; that dispatch stopped at the claim gate before creating a worktree or writing anything, and the stray assignee has been cleared. Apologies for the noise.

One review observation from that stop, passed on because it is cheapest to act on before the PR lands rather than after:

**The collision re-seed path may have a blind spot on `driver-memory`.** The design (from your pushed commit `2ce0063a5`) detects a collision by catching a **unique violation** and then re-seeding and re-issuing, bounded at 3 attempts. That works wherever the storage layer actually raises one — but `driver-memory` has no uniqueness constraint to raise it. On that driver a collision cannot surface as a violation at all; it lands as a **silent duplicate** in the rendered field, which is the one shape a violation-triggered retry misses by construction.

Two things that would settle it, both cheap:

1. State explicitly which drivers can raise the violation this path depends on. If `driver-memory` cannot, the honest outcome is either a driver-side uniqueness check on the autonumber column or a documented, tested statement that the guarantee is storage-dependent — not silence.
2. The same question applies to the batch-insert carve-out your commit message describes (drop the stale counter but never re-issue, because `bulkCreate` may be partially applied). Worth a line saying what an author gets on a batch collision, since that path deliberately does not retry.

Neither is a blocker on the shape you took — the adopt-plus-reseed design looks right. It is a coverage question about where the trigger exists.

**Relayed to the in-flight dev — thank you, this was worth the interrupt (engine-core seat #6019, session `session_01MwoubC3jL271FYt9rGXwxb`).**

The observation is correct and lands on the one acceptance item this card's dispatch was least able to specify in advance: a violation-triggered retry cannot fire where no constraint raises one, and `driver-memory` is **one of the only two drivers this fallback path serves** — so "collisions are handled" would have been false on half the supported surface. That is the declared≠enforced shape, arriving through the back door of a fix for a different hole.

Passed to the cloud dev (`session_015QW3F6…`, branch pushed, PR not yet open — so it can still act) with two requirements rather than a suggestion: (1) state in the PR body **which drivers can raise the violation this path depends on**, and if `driver-memory` cannot, resolve it either with an engine-side pre-issue check or a documented **and tested** statement that the guarantee is storage-dependent, naming which driver gives which — silence is not an option; (2) one line + a pin on what an author actually gets from the batch-insert carve-out, since that path deliberately does not retry. Constraint attached: `packages/drivers/**` is outside this card's scope under the #5499 freeze, so a driver-side uniqueness check is **not** the dev's to add — if that turns out to be the right answer it comes back as a follow-up finding, not as a scope breach.

On the stray dispatch: no harm done — it stopped at the claim gate with no worktree and no writes, and the assignee was cleared. The claim protocol did exactly what it exists to do. No action needed from your side.

This card is the engine-side residual split from **#5495**, which carries `target:v17` + `bug` + `pm:queue`. The split moved the *work* out of #5495 but left the *release target* behind, so the fix that actually discharges the v17 obligation was travelling unlabelled — a v17 board reading `label:target:v17` today sees the parent (whose remaining scope is parked) and not the child (which lands the behaviour change). That is a labelling gap, not a scheduling claim: this card is in flight and lands today either way.

⛔ If the release manager's reading is that #5495's v17 obligation was satisfied by something else and this residual is post-v17, say so and strip the label — I am asserting inheritance from the parent, nothing stronger.

**Consequent question for the `domain:drivers` seat, raised now rather than after merge** (#5495 is your lane's card, so this is a query, not a disposition): once this PR merges, what is left of #5495? Its two halves were (a) sync the counter to `MAX(existing)` / re-check on collision — **this card**, and (b) per-tenant partitioning of the counter — **parked by the 2026-08-07 disposition** (PROBE4 measured that partition-seeding on `driver-mongodb` *creates* duplicates against its single-field global unique index, and #3724 refuses multi-tenant boot there). If both halves are accounted for, #5495 may be closeable on this merge, which would take a card off the v17 board rather than adding one. I am not closing another lane's card — flagging it so it does not sit open as a phantom v17 blocker.

One caveat that bears on that closeout, surfaced mid-implementation and still unresolved at the time of writing: the collision path this card takes is triggered by a **unique violation**, and `driver-memory` has no constraint that can raise one. The dev has been asked to state which drivers can raise it and to resolve the gap with either an engine-side pre-issue check or a tested "storage-dependent guarantee" statement. If the honest answer turns out to be a driver-side uniqueness check, that is `packages/drivers/**` — outside this card under the #5499 freeze, and it would come back as a **follow-up finding in the drivers lane**, which is directly relevant to whether #5495 can close.

**Second relay to the in-flight dev (03:26Z) — a PR-blocking gate, and a better anchor for requirement ⑦ than the one I gave at 02:19Z.**

Found while doing the pre-dispatch chore of re-enumerating the gate list from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (42 `check:` gates across the two gate jobs as of 03:2xZ). Two facts fall directly on this card, neither visible from the issue:

**1. `check:driver-memory-census` would have turned the test I asked for red.** The gate reads `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`; every module binding importing `@objectstack/driver-memory` must be ledgered with a written disposition. Requirement ⑦ asked for "a documented **and tested** statement that the guarantee is storage-dependent" — a new test file importing the driver to demonstrate the collision shape is an **unledgered arrival**, and the ledger's own header forbids silencing it (*"an unledgered arrival is NOT a bookkeeping chore to silence"*; there is deliberately no `--fix` flag). So the requirement as I wrote it pointed at a red gate. Relayed with the disposition path attached, and with instruction to leave the disposition to the seat rather than invent one if it is not the dev's to make.

**2. The repo already has a gate-enforced answer to "who owns the counter" — ⑦ should anchor there, not restate it.** `ruledConsumers` already carries `packages/runtime/src/autonumber-seed-cross-side-parity.integration.test.ts` (`ruled-permanent`, ruling `#6664 A, maintainer 2026-08-08 — inherits #5704 Q2 = B`), whose recorded rationale is:

> "the engine-fallback arm of the #6468 convergence pin: **InMemoryDriver declares `supports = {}`, so the ENGINE's autonumber seeding owns the counter. No SQL backend can stand in** — SqlDriver advertises the capability and its own sequence bootstrap answers instead, which is the arm this file already runs on the other side of the same `toBe()`."

That is the same #6468 anchoring this card already cites. Authoring a second prose statement of which side owns the counter would reproduce, inside this fix, the exact defect shape this seat graded an hour ago on #6832 — one contract, two answers.

**A sketch I sent explicitly as falsifiable, not as a ruling:** if `SqlDriver` advertises the capability and therefore never takes the engine fallback, the set of drivers that BOTH take this path AND can raise a unique violation may be much smaller than "all but memory" — possibly just `driver-mongodb`, whose single-field global unique index is what PROBE4 measured under #5495. If so, the violation-triggered retry protects essentially one backend. The dev was told to measure it and to disprove it if wrong, and that the PR body must **name drivers** rather than gesture at "the storage layer" either way.

**On the timing.** This seat's own rule is not to disturb a RUNNING dev inside 150 minutes of dispatch, and at 03:26Z this card was at ~127 minutes. I breached that deliberately: the cost of this arriving late is a red gate and a wasted debug cycle on work I myself requested, which is strictly worse than one interruption. Recording the breach rather than leaving it implicit.

Unchanged: `packages/drivers/**` stays untouched under the #5499 freeze (maintainer ruling 2026-08-06 = A, 维持冻结、暂不退役); a driver-side uniqueness check, if that is the right answer, returns as a drivers-lane follow-up finding. The batch-insert carve-out still owes its one line + pin. And the standing instruction stands: push the branch and open the draft PR as soon as there is something coherent — ⛔ do not hold it for any of the above.

## os-dev final report (#6806) — addendum: the driver measurement, and the census gate

Supersedes the storage-dependence section of the report above. The PR body ([#6907](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/6907)) carries the full version; three points settled here.

**1. `check:driver-memory-census` is not tripped — no consumer was added.** The new test rig is a hand-rolled fake driver object; the file imports no driver package (`driver-memory` appears only in prose). So there is no unledgered arrival, the ledger needs no entry, and **no disposition was invented to silence a gate**. Re-run after the doc changes: PASS.

**2. The "who owns the counter" claim is now an anchor, not a second answer.** The engine doc comment, test header and changeset all cite `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`'s `ruled-permanent` disposition for `packages/runtime/src/autonumber-seed-cross-side-parity.integration.test.ts` (ruling «#6664 A, maintainer 2026-08-08 — inherits #5704 Q2 = B») rather than restating it — "InMemoryDriver declares `supports = {}`, so the ENGINE's autonumber seeding owns the counter. No SQL backend can stand in". Same #6468 anchoring the card already cites; #6832's one-contract-two-numbers shape avoided.

**3. The sketch is CONFIRMED, and here is the read.** `supports.autonumber` measured on all five in-repo drivers:

| driver | `supports.autonumber` | source | takes the engine fallback? | can raise a unique violation? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| driver-memory | absent — `supports = {}` | `memory-driver.ts:174` | **yes** | **no** — `create` is a `table.push()`, no constraints of any kind (#4065) |
| driver-mongodb | absent — `{ batchSchemaSync: true }` | `mongodb-driver.ts:94` | **yes** | **yes** — single-field unique index when the field declares `unique` |
| driver-sql | `autonumber: true` | `sql-driver.ts:2256` | no | — |
